name: code_analyze
description: Analyze source code: count lines, list functions/classes, check complexity, find TODOs. Language-aware analysis.

manual.overview: Use code_analyze to quickly understand a file or project structure: list all functions and classes, count lines, find TODOs, or check dependencies. Faster than reading the entire file.

examples.description: Find all TODOs in the project

tips: Use 'symbols' action first when exploring new code to get a map of the file.
The 'todos' action is great for finding unfinished work in a project.
Currently best supported for Python; other languages use basic heuristics.
edge_cases: Only Python files get full AST analysis (functions, classes, imports).
For other languages, the analysis uses regex-based heuristics.
Very large files may take a moment to parse.

executor.command: python -c "import ast, json, os, sys; path='{{args.path}}'; action='{{args.action}}'; code=open(path).read(); tree=ast.parse(code) if path.endswith('.py') else None; funcs=[n.name for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n,(ast.FunctionDef,ast.AsyncFunctionDef))] if tree else []; classes=[n.name for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n,ast.ClassDef)] if tree else []; lines=code.count('\n')+1; result={'file':path,'lines':lines,'functions':funcs,'classes':classes}; print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))"
